records.source: וּזְכֹר֙ אֶת־בּ֣וֹרְאֶ֔יךָ בִּימֵ֖י בְּחוּרֹתֶ֑יךָ עַ֣ד אֲשֶׁ֤ר לֹא־יָבֹ֨אוּ֙ יְמֵ֣י הָֽרָעָ֔ה וְהִגִּ֣יעוּ שָׁנִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֣ר תֹּאמַ֔ר אֵֽין־לִ֥י בָהֶ֖ם חֵֽפֶץ׃
records.gloss: And remember your Creator in [the] days of your youth, before that not come [the] days of the trouble and arrive years of which you will say, There is not to me in them pleasure,
pieces: Remember your Creator in the days of your youth, \q while the days of trouble have not yet come \q and the years have not drawn near when you will say, \q "I find no pleasure in them,"

L.1: And remember your Creator in the days of your youth, \q while the days of trouble have not [yet] come \q and the years [have not] arrived of which you will say, \q "I have no pleasure in them,"

R.1: Remember the God who made you while you are still young, \q before the hard days come, \q before the years arrive when you will say, \q "I do not enjoy life anymore."

decisions.choice: your Creator: God, who made you
alternatives: your well (your wife, as in Proverbs 5:15-18)
decisions.reason: The word is the participle of the verb used in Genesis 1:1 for God's creating. Its form is plural, which may be a plural of majesty, as "God" itself is plural in form. Because the letters are close to the words for "well" and "pit", some have read "remember your well" (your wife, as in Proverbs 5:15) or "remember your grave". The usual reading, "your Creator", fits the call to live before God (11:9; 12:7).

decisions.choice: the days of trouble: the hard days of old age
decisions.reason: The word (*ra'ah*) here is trouble or misfortune, not moral evil. The verses that follow picture those days.

decisions.choice: before: the start of one long sentence that runs to verse 7
decisions.reason: "Before" begins a series of pictures of old age and death, and comes back in verses 2 and 6. All of verses 1-7 hang on the command "remember your Creator". This poem closes Qoheleth's own words.

decisions.choice: I have no pleasure in them: there is no joy left in life
decisions.reason: The years of old age, when the strength to enjoy life is gone (2 Samuel 19:36).

decisions.choice: the God who made you
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly who the Creator is.

decisions.choice: a comma at the end of the verse
decisions.reason: The sentence goes on to verse 7, so Literal and Balanced end the verse with a comma. Readable makes shorter sentences.

records.heading: Remember your Creator

records.source: עַ֠ד אֲשֶׁ֨ר לֹֽא־תֶחְשַׁ֤ךְ הַשֶּׁ֨מֶשׁ֙ וְהָא֔וֹר וְהַיָּרֵ֖חַ וְהַכּוֹכָבִ֑ים וְשָׁ֥בוּ הֶעָבִ֖ים אַחַ֥ר הַגָּֽשֶׁם׃
records.gloss: before that not is darkened the sun and the light and the moon and the stars, and return the clouds after the rain,
pieces: before the sun grows dark, and the light, \q and the moon and the stars, \q and the clouds return after the rain,

L.2: before the sun is darkened, and the light, \q and the moon and the stars, \q and the clouds return after the rain,

R.2: Remember him before the sun and its light \q and the moon and the stars grow dark, \q and the clouds come back after the rain.

decisions.choice: the lights grow dark: the darkening of life as old age and death come near
alternatives: the darkness of the end of the world
decisions.reason: The sun, moon and stars going dark is the language the prophets use for the day of judgment (Isaiah 13:10; Joel 2:10). Here it pictures the end of one life: light and joy fade (11:7-8). Some read it more narrowly as failing eyesight, or as the dark days of winter.

decisions.choice: the clouds return after the rain: storm after storm, with no clearing
decisions.reason: In the land of Israel the rains come in winter. Clouds that return after the rain are the dreary days of winter, when one storm follows another. Old age is pictured as a winter with no spring after it.

decisions.choice: Remember him
decisions.reason: Readable starts a new sentence and repeats the command of verse 1, so that each sentence stands on its own.

records.source: בַּיּ֗וֹם שֶׁיָּזֻ֨עוּ֙ שֹׁמְרֵ֣י הַבַּ֔יִת וְהִֽתְעַוְּת֖וּ אַנְשֵׁ֣י הֶחָ֑יִל וּבָטְל֤וּ הַטֹּֽחֲנוֹת֙ כִּ֣י מִעֵ֔טוּ וְחָשְׁכ֥וּ הָרֹא֖וֹת בָּאֲרֻבּֽוֹת׃
records.gloss: in the day that tremble [the] keepers of the house, and bend [the] men of the strength, and cease the grinders because they are few, and are darkened those looking through the windows,
pieces: on the day when the guards of the house tremble \q and the strong men stoop, \q when the women who grind stop because they are few, \q and the women who look through the windows see only dimly,

L.3: in the day when the keepers of the house tremble, \q and the men of strength bend, \q and the grinding women stop because they are few, \q and those [women] who look through the windows grow dark,

R.3: That is when the guards of the house will tremble \q and the strong men will be bent over. \q The women who grind the grain will stop, because there are only a few of them, \q and the women who look out the windows will hardly see.

decisions.choice: the house: a great house falling into decay and silence, a picture of old age and death
alternatives: the body of an old person: arms, legs, teeth and eyes
a household in mourning after a death
a city or community in decline
decisions.reason: Verses 3-5 picture a large house where everything is failing: the guards tremble, the strong men stoop, the women who grind grain stop, the women at the windows can no longer see, the doors are shut and the sound of the mill dies away. Readers have long differed on what the picture means. An old reading, both Jewish and Christian, takes each part as a part of the aging body: the keepers are the arms and hands, the strong men the legs, the grinders the teeth, those at the windows the eyes, the doors the ears or lips. Others read it as a real household struck by death, or as a picture of decline in general. The translation keeps the pictures as the poem gives them.

decisions.choice: the grinders: the women who grind grain at the hand mill
decisions.reason: The word is feminine. Grinding grain each morning at a hand mill was women's work (Exodus 11:5). On the reading of the house as the body, the grinders are the teeth, few and no longer able to chew. This is one of the images on which readers differ (m1).

decisions.choice: those who look through the windows grow dark: the women at the windows can no longer see
decisions.reason: The participle is feminine: women looking out of the lattice windows (Judges 5:28). Their growing dark is often read as the eyes losing their sight.

decisions.choice: the keepers of the house and the men of strength: the guards and the strong men of the household
decisions.reason: The keepers protect the house; the strong men carry its burdens. They tremble and stoop. On the reading of the house as the body, they are the hands and arms, and the legs.

decisions.choice: the grinding women ... those [women] who look (L); the women who grind ... the women who look (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew words are feminine (m2, m3), so the renderings say "women". They keep the pictures and do not choose between the readings in m1.

records.source: וְסֻגְּר֤וּ דְלָתַ֨יִם֙ בַּשּׁ֔וּק בִּשְׁפַ֖ל ק֣וֹל הַֽטַּחֲנָ֑ה וְיָקוּם֙ לְק֣וֹל הַצִּפּ֔וֹר וְיִשַּׁ֖חוּ כָּל־בְּנ֥וֹת הַשִּֽׁיר׃
records.gloss: and are shut [the] doors in the street, when [is] low [the] sound of the grinding, and one rises at [the] sound of the bird, and are brought low all [the] daughters of the song,
pieces: when the doors on the street are closed \q and the noise of grinding fades, \q when people rise at the sound of a bird, \q and all the songs grow faint,

L.4: and the doors on the street are shut, \q when the sound of the grinding is low, \q and one rises at the sound of the bird, \q and all the daughters of song are brought low,

R.4: The doors to the street will be closed, \q and the sound of the mill will grow quiet. \q People will wake up when a bird sings, \q and all the songs will fade away.

decisions.choice: the doors shut and the sound of grinding low: the house falls silent
alternatives: the ears grow deaf, or the lips close over toothless gums
decisions.reason: The doors of the house onto the street are closed, and the daily sound of the mill dies away. On the reading of the house as the body (verse 3), the doors are the ears or the lips, and the faint grinding is the chewing of an old mouth. See the main note on the images of the poem at verse 3.

decisions.choice: one rises at the sound of the bird: the old wake at the first birdsong
alternatives: the voice rises to the thin pitch of a bird
the bird's voice rises (in a funeral lament)
decisions.reason: The verb has no clear subject. It is most often read as the old person waking at the first bird of dawn, unable to sleep. Others read that the voice of the old becomes thin like a bird's, or that the sound of a bird rises over the silent house.

decisions.choice: the daughters of song: songs, or singing women
decisions.reason: "Daughters of" can name the members of a group, so "daughters of song" may be the notes of songs or the women who sing them. They are "brought low": they grow faint, perhaps because the old can no longer hear them (2 Samuel 19:36).

decisions.choice: all the songs grow faint (B); all the songs will fade away (R)
alternatives: all the daughters of song are brought low
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the idiom means (m3). Literal keeps the Hebrew phrase.

decisions.choice: people rise (B); people will wake up (R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has no stated subject (m2). Balanced and Readable say "people", which keeps the most common reading without naming a body part.

records.source: גַּ֣ם מִגָּבֹ֤הַּ יִרָ֨אוּ֙ וְחַתְחַתִּ֣ים בַּדֶּ֔רֶךְ וְיָנֵ֤אץ הַשָּׁקֵד֙ וְיִסְתַּבֵּ֣ל הֶֽחָגָ֔ב וְתָפֵ֖ר הָֽאֲבִיּוֹנָ֑ה כִּֽי־הֹלֵ֤ךְ הָאָדָם֙ אֶל־בֵּ֣ית עוֹלָמ֔וֹ וְסָבְב֥וּ בָשּׁ֖וּקהַסֹּפְדִֽים׃
records.gloss: also of height they are afraid, and terrors [are] in the way, and blossoms the almond, and drags itself along the grasshopper, and fails the caper-berry; for goes the human to [the] house of his eternity, and go around in the street the mourners,
pieces: when people are afraid of heights and of dangers on the road, \q when the almond tree blossoms and the grasshopper drags itself along, \q and the caper-berry no longer stirs desire, \q because everyone goes to their eternal home, \q and mourners go about in the streets,

L.5: also of a height they are afraid, and terrors [are] on the way, \q and the almond tree blossoms, and the grasshopper drags itself along, \q and the caper-berry fails; \q for {{gender:the human|man}} goes to {{gender:their|his}} eternal house, \q and the mourners go around in the street,

R.5: People will be afraid of high places and of dangers in the street. \q The almond tree will blossom, and the grasshopper will drag itself along, \q and desire will be gone. \q All this happens because people are going to their everlasting home, \q and mourners walk around in the streets.

decisions.choice: the almond tree blossoms: perhaps the white hair of age
alternatives: spring returns while the old person fades
decisions.reason: The almond tree blooms in late winter with white blossoms. Many read it as white hair. Others take it as a sign of new life in nature, set against a human life that is ending.

decisions.choice: the grasshopper drags itself along: a creature made to leap that can only crawl
alternatives: the grasshopper is a burden (even something light weighs heavy)
decisions.reason: The verb can mean to drag oneself along or to be a burden. The grasshopper, which normally springs, moves slowly and stiffly, like the old. Or even a grasshopper becomes too heavy to carry.

decisions.choice: the caper-berry fails: appetite and desire fade
decisions.reason: The word (*'aviyonah*) appears only here. It is usually taken as the caper-berry, which was eaten to stir appetite and desire; the ancient Greek translation has "the caper". The word also looks like the word for "desire". Either way, the appetite for life is gone.

decisions.choice: his eternal house: the grave
decisions.reason: The grave is a person's lasting home (Psalm 49:12). The house of the poem gives way to the house no one leaves.

decisions.choice: the mourners go around in the street: the funeral is being prepared
decisions.reason: Mourners, some of them hired, walked through the streets wailing at a death (Jeremiah 9:16-17; Amos 5:16).

decisions.choice: they are afraid of a height: the old fear high places and the dangers of the road
decisions.reason: The subject is not named; it is the people of the house, the old. A climb or a walk outside becomes frightening.

decisions.choice: desire will be gone
decisions.reason: Readable says what the image means (m3), since the plant is unknown to most readers. Literal and Balanced keep the caper-berry.

decisions.choice: everyone ... their (B); people ... their (R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word means a human being; Balanced and Readable speak of everyone. Literal keeps the singular with the gender setting.

records.source: עַ֣ד אֲשֶׁ֤ר לֹֽא־יֵרָתֵק֙ חֶ֣בֶל הַכֶּ֔סֶף וְתָרֻ֖ץ גֻּלַּ֣ת הַזָּהָ֑ב וְתִשָּׁ֤בֶר כַּד֙ עַל־הַמַּבּ֔וּעַ וְנָרֹ֥ץ הַגַּלְגַּ֖ל אֶל־הַבּֽוֹר׃
records.gloss: before that not is snapped [the] cord of the silver, and is crushed [the] bowl of the gold, and is shattered [the] jar at the spring, and is crushed the wheel at the cistern,
pieces: before the silver cord is snapped \q and the golden bowl is broken, \q before the jar is shattered at the spring \q and the wheel broken at the well,

L.6: before the cord of silver is snapped, \q and the bowl of gold is crushed, \q and the jar is shattered at the spring, \q and the wheel is crushed at the cistern,

R.6: Remember him before the silver cord snaps \q and the golden bowl breaks, \q before the jar is smashed at the spring \q and the wheel at the well is broken.

decisions.choice: the silver cord and the golden bowl: a precious lamp falls and its light goes out
alternatives: parts of the body, such as the spine and the skull
a single picture of a golden lamp hanging by a silver chain
decisions.reason: The silver cord and the golden bowl are most often read as a lamp, its oil bowl hanging by a silver chain (compare the bowl of the lampstand in Zechariah 4:2-3). When the cord breaks, the bowl falls, and the light goes out: life ends. The costly metals show how precious life is. Some read the cord and bowl as parts of the body, as with the house of verse 3.

decisions.choice: the jar at the spring and the wheel at the cistern: water can no longer be drawn
decisions.reason: The jar for carrying water is broken at the spring, and the wheel or pulley for lowering a bucket is broken at the cistern. Water, the source of life, can no longer be drawn. Readers who see the body here take them as organs such as the heart.

decisions.choice: is snapped, as the scribes read it
decisions.reason: The written Hebrew text has a verb meaning "is removed" or "is far off"; the scribes' reading in the margin, which differs by one letter, is "is snapped". The read form fits the picture of the cord.

decisions.choice: before: the third "before", taking up the command of verse 1
decisions.reason: The long sentence returns to "before" (verses 1 and 2) for its last pictures.

decisions.choice: Remember him
decisions.reason: As in verse 2, Readable repeats the command of verse 1 to start a new sentence.

decisions.choice: well
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "well", the familiar word for a place where water is drawn with a wheel and bucket. Literal keeps "cistern".

records.source: וְיָשֹׁ֧ב הֶעָפָ֛ר עַל־הָאָ֖רֶץ כְּשֶׁהָיָ֑ה וְהָר֣וּחַ תָּשׁ֔וּב אֶל־הָאֱלֹהִ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר נְתָנָֽהּ׃
records.gloss: and returns the dust to the earth as it was, and the spirit returns to the God who gave it.
pieces: and the dust goes back to the earth it came from, \q and the spirit returns to God, who gave it.

L.7: and the dust returns upon the earth as it was, \q and the spirit returns to the God who gave it.

R.7: Then the body will go back to the dust it came from, \q and the spirit will go back to God, who gave it.

decisions.choice: dust to the earth, spirit to God: creation undone
decisions.reason: God formed the first human from dust and breathed into him the breath of life (Genesis 2:7), and said, "to dust you shall return" (Genesis 3:19). At death the two part: the body returns to the earth, and the life God gave returns to him (Psalm 104:29; Job 34:14-15).

decisions.choice: the spirit: the breath of life that God gives
decisions.reason: The word (*ruach*) is breath, wind or spirit. Here it is the life God breathes into a person. Earlier Qoheleth asked who knows whether the human spirit goes upward (3:21); here he says it returns to God who gave it. The verse says where life comes from and goes; it does not describe what lies beyond. Readers differ on how much more it implies.

decisions.choice: and: the last line of the poem
decisions.reason: This verse ends the long sentence begun in verse 1, and Qoheleth's own words, which began in 1:12.

decisions.choice: the spirit
decisions.reason: "Spirit" at every level, as in 3:19-21, so that *ruach* is never confused with *hevel*, which this book renders "breath". What the spirit is here, the life God gives, is said in m2.

decisions.choice: the body ... the dust it came from
decisions.reason: Readable names what the dust stands for: the body made from dust.

records.source: הֲבֵ֧ל הֲבָלִ֛ים אָמַ֥ר הַקּוֹהֶ֖לֶת הַכֹּ֥ל הָֽבֶל׃
records.gloss: Breath of breaths, says the Qoheleth; the all [is] breath.
pieces: Breath upon breath, says the Teacher. Everything is a breath.

L.8: Breath of breaths, says Qoheleth; everything [is] breath.

R.8: Nothing lasts! says the Teacher. Everything passes like a breath.

decisions.choice: breath of breaths: the cry that opened the book, repeated at its close
decisions.reason: The verse repeats 1:2 in a shorter form. Qoheleth's words begin and end with the same cry, and everything between is framed by it. See the main note on *hevel* at 1:2.

decisions.choice: breath of breaths: the most fleeting breath, utter breath
decisions.reason: Putting a word with its own plural is a Hebrew way of saying "the most" or "the greatest" ("the Song of Songs", "the holy of holies"). See 1:2.

decisions.choice: says Qoheleth: the frame of the book speaks again
decisions.reason: Here the voice that introduced Qoheleth in 1:1-2 speaks of him again in the third person, and goes on doing so to the end of the book (verses 9-14). The name here has the article, "the Qoheleth", as if it were a title (compare 7:27).

decisions.choice: Breath of breaths ... everything is breath (L); Breath upon breath ... Everything is a breath (B); Nothing lasts! Everything passes like a breath (R)
decisions.reason: The founder's settled wording for the cry of 1:2 and 12:8, in the same words as 1:2 at each level. The shorter verse leaves out the repeated "breath of breaths" ("Nothing lasts!" at Readable).

decisions.choice: Qoheleth (L); the Teacher (B, R)
decisions.reason: The book-wide wording for *qohelet* (see 1:1). Literal keeps it as a name, without the article. No quotation marks are used, as at 1:2.

records.source: וְיֹתֵ֕ר שֶׁהָיָ֥ה קֹהֶ֖לֶת חָכָ֑ם ע֗וֹד לִמַּד־דַּ֨עַת֙ אֶת־הָעָ֔ם וְאִזֵּ֣ן וְחִקֵּ֔ר תִּקֵּ֖ן מְשָׁלִ֥ים הַרְבֵּֽה׃
records.gloss: And further, that was Qoheleth wise, still he taught knowledge the people, and he weighed and searched out [and] set in order proverbs many.
pieces: Besides being wise, the Teacher also taught the people knowledge. He weighed and studied and arranged many proverbs.

L.9: And further, besides Qoheleth being wise, he also taught the people knowledge; and he weighed and searched out [and] set in order many proverbs.

R.9: The Teacher was wise, and he also taught the people what he knew. He listened to many wise sayings, studied them, and put them in order.

decisions.choice: Qoheleth in the third person: the book's closing frame begins
decisions.reason: From here to the end of the book (verses 9-14) someone other than Qoheleth speaks about him: "Qoheleth was wise ... Qoheleth sought." The voice is the one that introduced him in 1:1-2 and spoke briefly in 7:27 and 12:8. It looks back on his work and gives the reader a last word of advice. Like Qoheleth's own words, it takes no quotation marks.

decisions.choice: further: besides, in addition
decisions.reason: The word (*yoter*) is related to "gain" (1:3). Here it means "in addition", as in verse 12.

decisions.choice: weighed: tested and judged
decisions.reason: The verb is related to the word for "ear" and to scales. It may mean that Qoheleth listened carefully to proverbs, or that he weighed them. Either way he judged their worth.

decisions.choice: set in order many proverbs: the work of a wise man and collector
decisions.reason: Solomon is said to have spoken many proverbs (1 Kings 5:12), and Proverbs gathers collections of sayings (Proverbs 1:1; 25:1). Qoheleth did the same kind of work.

decisions.choice: taught the people: taught the public, not only students
decisions.reason: His teaching was for ordinary people, as his name, one who addresses an assembly, suggests (see 1:1).

decisions.choice: Qoheleth (L); the Teacher (B, R)
decisions.reason: The book-wide wording for *qohelet* (see 1:1).

decisions.choice: listened to
decisions.reason: Readable gives the sense "listened" from m3, and adds "studied" for the second verb; Literal and Balanced keep "weighed".

records.source: בִּקֵּ֣שׁ קֹהֶ֔לֶת לִמְצֹ֖א דִּבְרֵי־חֵ֑פֶץ וְכָת֥וּב יֹ֖שֶׁר דִּבְרֵ֥י אֱמֶֽת׃
records.gloss: Sought Qoheleth to find words of delight, and written uprightly, words of truth.
pieces: The Teacher sought to find pleasing words, and to write honestly words of truth.

L.10: Qoheleth sought to find words of delight, and [what was] written uprightly, words of truth.

R.10: The Teacher tried to find just the right words. What he wrote was honest and true.

decisions.choice: words of delight: pleasing, well-chosen words
decisions.reason: The phrase means words that please (Proverbs 15:26; 16:24). Qoheleth cared how he said things, not only what he said.

decisions.choice: written uprightly: what he wrote was right
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has a passive form, "[what was] written", where a verb is expected. The sense is that Qoheleth wrote honestly. His words were both pleasing and true.

decisions.choice: words of truth: reliable words
decisions.reason: Truth here is what can be relied on (Proverbs 22:21).

decisions.choice: Qoheleth (L); the Teacher (B, R)
decisions.reason: The book-wide wording for *qohelet* (see 1:1).

records.source: דִּבְרֵ֤י חֲכָמִים֙ כַּדָּ֣רְבֹנ֔וֹת וּֽכְמַשְׂמְר֥וֹת נְטוּעִ֖ים בַּעֲלֵ֣י אֲסֻפּ֑וֹת נִתְּנ֖וּ מֵרֹעֶ֥ה אֶחָֽד׃
records.gloss: Words of wise [ones are] like the goads, and like nails firmly planted [are] masters of collections; they are given from shepherd one.
pieces: The words of the wise are like goads, and the collected sayings are like nails driven firmly in; they are given by one shepherd.

L.11: [The] words of [the] wise [are] like goads, and like nails firmly planted [are the] masters of collections; they are given by one shepherd.

R.11: The words of wise people are like the sharp sticks used to drive cattle. Their collected sayings are like nails driven in firmly. They are given by one shepherd.

decisions.choice: goads: pointed sticks for driving oxen
decisions.reason: A goad was a long stick with a sharp point, used to keep oxen moving (1 Samuel 13:21; Judges 3:31). The words of the wise prod people to think and act.

decisions.choice: like nails firmly planted: sayings that stay fixed in the mind
decisions.reason: The word means nails or pegs. Driven in deep, they hold firm. Wise sayings stay in the memory and give stability.

decisions.choice: masters of collections: collected sayings, or those who collect them
decisions.reason: The phrase is unusual. It can mean "collected sayings", or the people skilled in collecting them, or "masters of assemblies", the teachers who address gatherings. All the readings point to the work described in verse 9.

decisions.choice: one shepherd: God, the source of wisdom, or one teacher
decisions.reason: "Shepherd" is used of God (Psalm 23:1; 80:2) and of kings and leaders (Jeremiah 23:4). Many read "one shepherd" as God, the one source of all true wisdom (Proverbs 2:6). Others read it as a single teacher, perhaps the king who gathered the sayings. The translation keeps "one shepherd" and does not decide.

decisions.choice: one shepherd (lowercase)
decisions.reason: The word is kept lowercase at every level because it is not certain that it refers to God (m4).

decisions.choice: the sharp sticks used to drive cattle
decisions.reason: Readable explains the goad (m1), which few readers have seen.

records.source: וְיֹתֵ֥ר מֵהֵ֖מָּה בְּנִ֣י הִזָּהֵ֑ר עֲשׂ֨וֹת סְפָרִ֤ים הַרְבֵּה֙ אֵ֣ין קֵ֔ץ וְלַ֥הַג הַרְבֵּ֖ה יְגִעַ֥ת בָּשָֽׂר׃
records.gloss: And further, from these, my son, be warned: making books many there is no end, and study much [is] weariness of flesh.
pieces: Beyond these, my son, take warning: the making of many books never ends, and much study wears out the body.

L.12: And further, from these, my son, be warned: making many books, [there is] no end [to it], and much study [is] a weariness of flesh.

R.12: My son, be careful about anything beyond these words. People will never stop writing books, and too much study will wear you out.

decisions.choice: further, from these: beyond these words of the wise
decisions.reason: The words most likely warn against going beyond the sayings of the wise (verse 11): there is no end to books. Some read "by these": let these words warn you.

decisions.choice: my son: a teacher speaking to a pupil
decisions.reason: The address is the one Proverbs uses for a teacher's words to a learner (Proverbs 1:8).

decisions.choice: study: devotion to books, much reading
decisions.reason: The word appears only here in the Hebrew Bible. It seems to mean study or poring over books.

decisions.choice: my son
decisions.reason: As in Proverbs 1:8, the address to the learner is kept as "my son" at every level.

decisions.choice: wears out the body (B); will wear you out (R)
alternatives: is a weariness of the flesh
decisions.reason: "Flesh" here means the body.

records.source: ס֥וֹף דָּבָ֖ר הַכֹּ֣ל נִשְׁמָ֑ע אֶת־הָאֱלֹהִ֤ים יְרָא֙ וְאֶת־מִצְוֺתָ֣יו שְׁמ֔וֹר כִּי־זֶ֖ה כָּל־הָאָדָֽם׃
records.gloss: [The] end of [the] matter, the all has been heard: the God fear, and his commandments keep, for this [is the] whole of the human.
pieces: Here is the end of the matter, now that all has been heard: Fear God and keep {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} commandments, because this is the whole of being human.

L.13: [The] end of [the] matter, everything having been heard: fear God and keep {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} commandments, for this [is] all of {{gender:humankind|man}}.

R.13: Now everything has been said, and here is the conclusion: Honor God with awe and keep {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} commandments. That is what life is all about for every person.

decisions.choice: the end of the matter, all has been heard: the conclusion, now that everything has been said
alternatives: when all has been heard, the end of the matter is this
decisions.reason: The words sum up the book. "The end of the matter" is the last word; "all has been heard" means that everything has now been said and considered.

decisions.choice: fear God: the book's last word
decisions.reason: To fear God is to live in reverent awe of him, as in 3:14 (see the main note there), 5:6, 7:18 and 8:12-13. The book ends where Proverbs begins (Proverbs 1:7).

decisions.choice: keep his commandments: obey the commands God has given
decisions.reason: This is the only time the book speaks of God's commandments. The word is the one used for the king's command in 8:5, and for the commandments of the law (Deuteronomy 6:2; 10:12-13).

decisions.choice: this is the whole of humankind: this is what a human being is for
alternatives: this is the whole duty of everyone
decisions.reason: The Hebrew is brief: "this is the whole of humankind". It may mean that this is the whole of what a person should be and do, or that this is for every person. The words add no noun such as "duty".

decisions.choice: Honor God with awe
decisions.reason: The book-wide wording for "fear God" at Readable (see 3:14), as Proverbs 1:7 has it.

decisions.choice: the whole of being human (B); what life is all about for every person (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable keep both senses in m4 open as far as they can, and add no word such as "duty".

records.source: כִּ֤י אֶת־כָּל־מַֽעֲשֶׂ֔ה הָאֱלֹהִ֛ים יָבִ֥א בְמִשְׁפָּ֖ט עַ֣ל כָּל־נֶעְלָ֑ם אִם־ט֖וֹב וְאִם־רָֽע׃
records.gloss: For every deed the God will bring into judgment, concerning every hidden [thing], whether good or whether evil.
pieces: For God will bring every deed into judgment, including everything hidden, whether it is good or evil.

L.14: For every deed God will bring into judgment, with every hidden [thing], whether good or evil.

R.14: God will judge everything people do, even what is done in secret, whether it is good or bad.

decisions.choice: God will bring every deed into judgment
decisions.reason: The book has already said that God will judge the righteous and the wicked (3:17) and the young who enjoy their youth (11:9). It ends with the same truth: nothing is outside God's judgment.

decisions.choice: every hidden thing: all that is done in secret
decisions.reason: God sees what others cannot (Psalm 90:8; 139:1-12).

decisions.choice: good or evil: right and wrong
decisions.reason: Here the pair is moral, what is right and wrong, not good and bad times as in 7:14.

decisions.choice: the last word of the book
decisions.reason: When Ecclesiastes is read aloud in the synagogue, verse 13 is read again after verse 14, so that the reading does not end on the word "evil". The text itself ends here.

decisions.choice: bad
decisions.reason: Readable says "good or bad", the plain pair for right and wrong.
